title: Keep food safe and cook without power
short: Fridge and freezer in an outage, safe cooking, emergency food
intro: Readings for when the power or gas is out: how long fridge and freezer food stays safe, what to throw away, how to cook without burning or poisoning anyone, and how to make stored food last.

limits.text: Throw away refrigerated food that has been at 40 °F or higher for more than 4 hours, or that has an unusual odor, color or texture.
Discard perishable food that has been above 40 °F for 2 hours or more; you cannot rely on appearance or odor.
Use generators, camp stoves and charcoal grills only outdoors, at least 20 feet from windows, doors or garages; never heat a home with a gas stove, oven, grill or dryer.
Replace refrigerated medicines if the power is out a day or more unless the label says otherwise; call a doctor or pharmacist if you depend on them.
Do not eat any food that may have touched flood water unless it is in a waterproof container that can be cleaned.
Food can be rationed safely for healthy adults, but not for children and pregnant women; water should not be rationed.
CDC advice is to discard any home-canned food that might contain botulism toxin.
